drafted_from: tool:read-a-servers-tls-certificate's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check how the certificate for app.example.com stands on my server at 192.0.2.34, signing in as admin." It runs tool:read-a-servers-tls-certificate, changes nothing and needs no DNS key.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-a-servers-tls-certificate and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.

3. Read what comes back: certificate_present, system_trust_and_hostname_verified, not_before_local, not_after_local, issuer, serial and private_key_mode (0600); with no certificate yet only {"hostname", "certificate_present": false}. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).
4. When not_after_local is close, run tool:renew-a-tls-certificate; when certificate_present is false run tool:issue-a-tls-certificate.

worked_examples.title: Read a live certificate
worked_examples.ask: How does the certificate for app.example.com stand?
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/do-work/tls-host-owner.py (certificate_status: openssl verify against the system CA list with the host name, a day left, key mode 0600); the server already holds a certificate for app.example.com.
